narrative.overview:
CHAK Content Radar extends the existing CHAK identity into a focused internal editorial desk. Warm paper tones and dark ink give the workspace the familiarity of marked-up briefs, while tomato red remains the decisive brand voice for generation, selection, and urgent editorial attention.

The interface is compact, operational, and evidence-led. Thin dividers, modest corner rounding, small status labels, and dense information blocks help editors scan sources, risk, scores, and production state without turning the workspace into a decorative marketing dashboard. The fixed carousel templates are part of this system: AI supplies constrained copy, while code preserves layout, hierarchy, and publish safety.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper surfaces anchored by a near-black editorial sidebar.
Tomato red used as a precise action and brand signal, not ambient decoration.
Compact, Korean-first typography with strong numeric and status hierarchy.
Evidence, verification, and publishing state remain visible beside creation controls.
Code-owned 4:5 carousel templates keep generated output structurally consistent.

rules.name: The One Red Decision Rule
rules.body: Tomato red marks the strongest brand or action decision in a region; it does not flood general surfaces.

rules.name: The Meaning Before Hue Rule
rules.body: Blue, green, ochre, and butter retain stable operational meanings and always appear with text or icon reinforcement.

rules.name: The Dense, Never Tiny Rule
rules.body: Use the compact label scale for supporting information, but preserve clear weight, contrast, and a larger touch target around it.

rules.name: The Canvas Scales Itself Rule
rules.body: Carousel typography uses container-relative units so the 4:5 composition keeps its hierarchy at thumbnail, preview, and export sizes.

rules.name: The Work First Rule
rules.body: The main task surface receives width first; contextual guidance remains narrow, sticky where useful, and collapses before the work area becomes cramped.

rules.name: The Flat Until Active Rule
rules.body: Resting cards use borders and tone; noticeable shadows appear only for interaction, hierarchy, preview focus, or transient feedback.

rules.name: The Radius Has Rank Rule
rules.body: Corner size increases with container scope: control, choice, card, then panel. Do not assign large floating radii to ordinary work surfaces.

dos: Do build hierarchy with paper tone, thin rules, weight, and compact spacing before adding shadow.
Do keep evidence, verification state, dates, and source actions adjacent to the editorial decision they affect.
Do preserve Pretendard-first Korean typography and container-relative type inside carousel canvases.
Do keep mobile icon controls at least 44px in each dimension and preserve visible keyboard focus.
Do use the four fixed carousel templates and their defined layout variants for generated output.
donts: Don't turn the workspace into a decorative marketing dashboard with gradients, glass panels, or oversized hero composition.
Don't use tomato red as a general background wash or apply it to multiple competing actions in one region.
Don't communicate verification, risk, or publish readiness through color alone.
Don't introduce freeform AI-designed layouts; copy and image choices may vary, but composition remains code-owned.
Don't add heavy shadows to resting cards or increase corner radii beyond the established control-to-panel hierarchy.
